content.title: Famed Bear Michael Burry Is Bullish on Fannie and Freddie
content.summary: In a 6,000-word blog post on Monday, Burry outlined why he’s now bullish on the government-sponsored enterprises, the political and regulatory hurdles that stand in the way of a public offering, and the steps he says Washington must take before the pair can stage a comeback on Wall Street.  Burry earned a reputation for predicting the collapse of the US housing market before the 2008 financial crisis.  While some investors have famously held Fannie and Freddie positions for over a decade, Burry said he became bullish on the shares only after President Donald Trump’s election last year.

content.title: Who Are the Key Players in a Fannie, Freddie IPO?
content.summary: The U.S. Treasury: A deal would likely involve the Treasury selling a portion of the stake it took in the firms in the 2008-09 financial crisis.  When the government put the firms under conservatorship, it wanted to ensure taxpayers—via the Treasury—were adequately repaid for the risk they took to stabilize the mortgage market.  Junior preferred shareholders: Below the senior preferred shares sit roughly $35 billion in outstanding junior preferred shares, according to a 2024 Congressional Budget Office report.
